chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When he sends his hunting dog and forgets to mention the name of God, it is in the same position as one who slaughtered [an animal] and forgot to mention the name of God; and likewise, when he throws an arrow and forgets to mention the name of God.

key_terms.يُسَمِّيَ: To mention the name of God (Tasmiyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunted game if the hunter forgets to say 'Bismillah'?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Zurarah to clarify the fiqh of *Tasmiyah* in hunting, equating the status of an animal hunted with a forgotten invocation to one slaughtered with a forgotten one. This ruling extends to archery, emphasizing that the validity of the catch depends on the intention and remembrance of God's name at the moment of release, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of game.
